intended_object: An equivalence of categories between finitely generated representations of the affine group scheme Spec H (given as natural actions on points) and finitely generated right H-comodules, for a commutative Hopf algebra H over a commutative ring R. This is the finite-dimensional case of the representation–comodule dictionary (Milne, ch. VIII). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes the library's full equivalence `toComodule.asEquivalence`, between point representations and comodules, and restricts it to full subcategories using `Equivalence.congrFullSubcategory`. This needs the two finite-generation properties to match: being finitely generated on the comodule side, pulled back along the functor, must equal being finitely generated on the representation side. Both properties are `Module.Finite R` of the same underlying module, and the library proves they agree with `Iff.rfl`, so the subcategories line up exactly.

The functor underneath is the standard one. It keeps the underlying module, turns the point action into a coaction, and keeps the linear maps on morphisms.

The setting is a commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative ring, which is the natural generality for affine group schemes. Over a field, finitely generated means finite-dimensional, which matches the docstring.

I found no comodule-category or representation–comodule equivalence in Mathlib to compare against, so there is no Mathlib counterpart and nothing more general there.
